question: On 255 exposed opponent-switch states, the fourth-round adaptive gate lost nine points to keeping the population expert active. Varying dwell time or hysteresis over 42 settings failed to improve its broad merit. Can learning which expert changes the ring-out result in the same state improve those choices?
intervention: Freeze both existing experts. The learned controller may use the same 37 terms as the original selector, consisting of a bias, 22 own-client features and seven pairs of slow averages and fast-minus-slow differences. Learn the signed ring-out score difference from exact counterfactual trials. Only the offline teacher sees continuations. Neither the solver nor the resulting gate receives the opponent name, future timing or server state as an input feature.
examples: Use all 16 training calendars, both seats, two symmetric RTTs and every exposed common-field fighter. Choose five elapsed-time bands before seeing the bout outcome. At the next input head after each surviving landmark force population or table for 3, 8 or 20 own input heads, then release to the current gate. Run matched plain W-tap and unchanged continuations from the same queued state and primed histories. The prefix stays identical up to the next legal decision. Scale examples by opponent so long-lived opponents do not dominate. Skip starts without another own input head and retain their counts. Preserve checks of unchanged branches and the two teachers' identical feature vectors.
iterations: Train three rounds. Start with the frozen adaptive gate and collect each next round on the best pair controller from the previous tournament. Fixed controls can win the overall title. Aggregate teacher samples from completed rounds before refitting. Use least-squares signed terminal advantage with three ridge penalties. Compare three levels of commitment to the original gate and three deadbands for the learned advantage. Select six distinct weight sets in training before competing with W-tap, Hold-W, the frozen adaptive, population, table and prior winners on eight exposed development calendars. Publish each true tournament winner and its best new entry immediately. Use the arithmetic mean of average points, worst-five and worst-opponent points; break ties by average then name. Report results separately against the additional legacy field.
transfer: Freeze one new contender independently of prospective outcomes. Compare the final new entry, incumbent adaptive, pure population and W-tap against W-tap, Hold-W, the three weakest exposed opponents of the challenger and the four reserved switchers. Give each equal competition settings including mouse control, both seats, 0/80 ms, two native repeats and eight prospective historical mirror tapes. This is an additional panel. It does not change the entrants or conclusions of the previously frozen title tournament. Within-match changes must earn an advantage over both fixed components before attributing gains to adaptation.
